# Rule register

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:rules` from the engine's rule entries (src/engine/registry.ts and src/engine/au/registry.ts). Do not edit by hand: test/docs/rule-register.test.ts fails when this file and the engine disagree. -->

Every rule the calculation engine carries, with its effective dates, the sources it was read from and how confident the engine's authors are in it. This is the same register as the app's **Rules & sources** workspace, and each rule's id is the one shown there and in calculation breakdowns.

How to read it:

* **Verified (primary source):** the rate, threshold or method was read from legislation or the tax authority's own guidance on the date shown against each source.
* **Verified (secondary source only):** corroborated by a reputable secondary source (for example a professional firm's summary) but not yet by a primary source. A reviewer should confirm it against the primary source.
* **Assumption:** a modelling choice or simplification. The app flags these for a tax professional's review, and the calculation documents explain each one.
* **Effective dates** are inclusive. A rule with no end date applies until further notice; the engine refuses to calculate for a date no rule covers rather than guessing.

The calculation documents in this folder explain how the rules are combined, with worked examples; start at [README.md](README.md).

## Australia

### <a id="area-au-au-capital-allowances"></a>AU capital allowances (9)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-div43-build-to-rent-2025-plus"></a>Build-to-rent Division 43 accelerated rate

* **Rule id:** `au-div43.build-to-rent.2025-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2025 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Eligible active build-to-rent development areas can claim 4% capital works deductions once the development is active and notified, provided construction began after 9 May 2023 and the federal BTR conditions are met.
* **Limits and notes:** The engine requires the user to supply the active BTR commencement date and assumes the project otherwise satisfies the single-owner, affordable-dwelling and 15-year compliance conditions.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO legal database | ITAA 1997 section 43-145](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=PAC/19970038/43-145) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Build-to-rent development tax incentives](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/assets-and-property/build-to-rent-development-tax-incentives) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [Federal Register of Legislation | Income Tax Assessment Act 1997](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A05138/latest/text) (Federal Register of Legislation, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-div40-general-formulas-2001-plus"></a>Division 40 decline in value formulas and balancing adjustments

* **Rule id:** `au-div40.general-formulas.2001-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2001 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Division 40 lets the holder deduct decline in value using the diminishing value or prime cost method. The numerator uses actual days held, but sections 40-70 and 40-75 keep the denominator at 365; a balancing adjustment compares termination value with adjustable value on disposal.
* **Limits and notes:** The module models the standard Division 40 formulas and ordinary balancing adjustments only; it does not attempt the specialised intangible-asset or rollover variants.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO legal database | ITAA 1997 section 40-25](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=PAC/19970038/40-25) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO legal database | ITAA 1997 section 40-70](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=PAC/19970038/40-70) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO legal database | ITAA 1997 section 40-75](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=PAC/19970038/40-75) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Depreciating assets guide 2025 - Working out decline in value](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/depreciating-assets-guide-2025/depreciating-assets-effective-life-cost-and-decline-in-value/working-out-decline-in-value) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Depreciating assets guide 2025 - What happens if you no longer hold or use a depreciating asset](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/depreciating-assets-guide-2025/what-happens-if-you-no-longer-hold-or-use-a-depreciating-asset) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [Federal Register of Legislation | Income Tax Assessment Act 1997](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A05138/latest/text) (Federal Register of Legislation, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-div43-general-rates-1979-plus"></a>Division 43 capital works deductions - general and 4% bands

* **Rule id:** `au-div43.general-rates.1979-plus`
* **Effective:** from 22 Aug 1979 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Division 43 covers buildings begun after 21 August 1979 and structural improvements begun after 26 February 1992. The core rate is 2.5% over 40 years, with 4% over 25 years for the pre-16 September 1987 band and modern industrial / traveller-accommodation 4% uses.
* **Limits and notes:** The engine models the core commencement-date / use tests and day apportionment. Complex quasi-ownership, R&amp;D and destruction claims need reviewed overrides.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO legal database | ITAA 1997 section 43-20](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=PAC/19970038/43-20) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO legal database | ITAA 1997 section 43-25](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=PAC/19970038/43-25) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO legal database | ITAA 1997 section 43-145](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=PAC/19970038/43-145) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Company tax return 2024 instructions - Appendix 3 capital works deductions](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/company-tax-return-2024-instructions/appendixes-for-the-company-tax-return/appendix-3-capital-works-deductions) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [Federal Register of Legislation | Income Tax Assessment Act 1997](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A05138/latest/text) (Federal Register of Legislation, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-div43-cost-base-2000-plus"></a>Division 43 deductions reduce CGT cost base

* **Rule id:** `au-div43.cost-base.2000-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2000 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Division 43 deductions do not trigger an ordinary sale balancing adjustment, but deductions claimed or claimable reduce the CGT cost base, including capital works expenditure incurred by a prior owner that the current owner can deduct.
* **Limits and notes:** Section 110-45(4) captures deductions for another entity's capital expenditure that the current owner can deduct under Division 43.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO legal database | ITAA 1997 section 110-45](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=PAC/19970038/110-45) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Cost base of an asset](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/cost-base-of-asset) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | CGT when selling your rental property](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/property-and-capital-gains-tax/cgt-when-selling-your-rental-property) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-div40-pools-and-small-business-2026"></a>Low-value pools and the small-business instant asset write-off

* **Rule id:** `au-div40.pools-and-small-business.2026`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2023 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Low-value pools use 18.75% for current-year low-cost additions and 37.5% for the opening pool balance. As at 10 October 2026, the instant asset write-off page still shows a $20,000 per-asset threshold from 1 July 2023 for entities with aggregated turnover below $10 million that use simplified depreciation rules.
* **Limits and notes:** The instant asset write-off remains targeted at small businesses using simplified depreciation. The engine does not assume ordinary property funds qualify.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Depreciating assets guide 2024 - Low-value pools](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/depreciating-assets-guide-2024/low-value-pools) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Instant asset write-off](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/depreciation-and-capital-expenses-and-allowances/simpler-depreciation-for-small-business/instant-asset-write-off) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | $20,000 instant asset write-off for 2025-26](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/small-business-newsroom/20000-instant-asset-write-off-for-2025-26) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Small business pool calculations](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/depreciation-and-capital-expenses-and-allowances/simpler-depreciation-for-small-business/small-business-pool-calculations) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-div40-second-hand-residential-2017-plus"></a>Second-hand depreciating assets in residential accommodation

* **Rule id:** `au-div40.second-hand-residential.2017-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2017 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Section 40-27 denies decline-in-value deductions for many second-hand assets used to provide residential accommodation unless an exception applies, but the exempt entity list includes corporate tax entities, non-SMSF super funds, public unit trusts, MITs and wholly-eligible unit trusts or partnerships.
* **Limits and notes:** The module models the main section 40-27 exceptions but leaves unusual 'new residential premises' fact patterns for manual review.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO legal database | ITAA 1997 section 40-27](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=PAC/19970038/40-27) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Second-hand depreciating assets](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/property-and-land/residential-rental-properties/rental-expenses/depreciating-assets-in-rental-properties/second-hand-depreciating-assets) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Rental properties 2026 - Descriptions and examples of rental property items](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/rental-properties-2026/residential-rental-property-assets/descriptions-and-examples-of-rental-property-items) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-borrowing-expenses-25-25"></a>Section 25-25 borrowing expenses

* **Rule id:** `au-borrowing-expenses.25-25`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 1997 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Borrowing expenses are deducted over the shorter of 5 years and the actual loan period, unless the deductible amount is $100 or less in the year incurred. The statutory method recalculates the remaining expenditure by reference to the remaining loan period each year, so early repayment accelerates the final claim.
* **Limits and notes:** The module returns cents and assumes the caller has already identified the deductible portion of mixed-purpose borrowings via taxableUseBps.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO legal database | ITAA 1997 section 25-25](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=PAC/19970038/25-25) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Borrowing expenses](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/property-and-land/residential-rental-properties/rental-expenses/borrowing-expenses) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [Federal Register of Legislation | Income Tax Assessment Act 1997](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A05138/latest/text) (Federal Register of Legislation, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-blackhole-expenditure-40-880"></a>Section 40-880 business-related capital expenditure

* **Rule id:** `au-blackhole-expenditure.40-880`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2005 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Section 40-880 generally spreads eligible business-related capital expenditure over 5 income years starting in the year incurred, provided the expenditure is not otherwise deductible or included in a depreciating asset, land, lease/right or CGT cost base.
* **Limits and notes:** This module is limited to the standard five-year rule in section 40-880(2); the immediate start-up deduction for qualifying smaller businesses is left to manual review.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO legal database | ITAA 1997 section 40-880](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=PAC/19970038/40-880) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [Federal Register of Legislation | Income Tax Assessment Act 1997](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A05138/latest/text) (Federal Register of Legislation, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-div40-property-asset-lives-2026"></a>Verified effective lives loaded into the property asset catalogue

* **Rule id:** `au-div40.property-asset-lives.2026`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2019 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** The asset catalogue only assigns defaults where the ATO rental-property tables or air-conditioning / machinery tables state an effective life for assets acquired on or after the stated column date. Assets without a verified table entry leave defaultEffectiveLifeYears undefined so the caller must supply a reviewed life.
* **Limits and notes:** The loaded defaults are intentionally conservative and only apply from the stated acquisition date for each asset class. If the asset predates that column, the calculator warns and the user should enter an explicit effective life. If the current Commissioner's table says 'own estimate' or the asset is not listed, the engine requires user input.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Rental properties 2026 - Residential rental property items](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/rental-properties-2026/residential-rental-property-assets/residential-rental-property-items) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Rental properties 2026 - Common rental property items](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/rental-properties-2026/residential-rental-property-assets/common-rental-property-items) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

### <a id="area-au-au-cgt"></a>AU CGT (3)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-cgt-cost-base-and-discount"></a>CGT cost base, discount and indexation methods

* **Rule id:** `au-cgt.cost-base-and-discount`
* **Effective:** from 21 Sep 1999 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** The cost base comprises five elements, but deductible amounts are excluded and Division 43 deductions reduce the cost base. The CGT discount is generally 50% for individuals and trusts and 33 1/3% for complying super funds if the asset was acquired at least 12 months before the CGT event; indexation remains available for pre-21 September 1999 acquisitions.
* **Limits and notes:** The engine focuses on straightforward CGT event A1 style disposals of real property or units. It does not attempt the full catalogue of rollover and special-event rules.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Cost base of an asset](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/calculating-your-cgt/cost-base-of-asset) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

  * [ATO legal database | ITAA 1997 section 110-45](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=PAC/19970038/110-45) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO legal database | ITAA 1997 section 115-25](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?docid=PAC/19970038/115-25) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Capital gains tax guide 2021 - The discount method](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/capital-gains-tax-guide-2021/whats-new/how-to-work-out-your-capital-gain-or-capital-loss/the-discount-method) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-frcgw-2016-plus"></a>Foreign resident capital gains withholding

* **Rule id:** `au-frcgw.2016-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2016 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** FRCGW applies to direct real property, relevant indirect Australian real property interests and relevant options or rights unless an exclusion, clearance certificate, vendor declaration or variation applies. The statutory rates changed from 10% over a $2 million threshold (from 1 July 2016) to 12.5% over a $750,000 threshold (from 1 July 2017) and then to 15% for all property values from 1 January 2025.
* **Limits and notes:** The calculator gives the purchaser's withholding amount and settlement timing. It does not lodge the purchaser payment notification or allocate multi-vendor credits between related entities.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Foreign resident capital gains withholding overview](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/foreign-residents-and-capital-gains-tax/foreign-resident-capital-gains-withholding/foreign-resident-capital-gains-withholding-overview) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-cgt-loss-order-and-foreign-residents"></a>Loss ordering and foreign / temporary resident discount restrictions

* **Rule id:** `au-cgt.loss-order-and-foreign-residents`
* **Effective:** from 9 May 2012 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Current-year and prior-year capital losses are used before any discount. For individuals, the foreign / temporary resident rules apportion the discount by reference to eligible Australian-resident days after 8 May 2012; foreign residents disregard gains on non-taxable-Australian-property assets altogether.
* **Limits and notes:** Trust beneficiary level apportionment under sections 115-110 / 115-120 is left to the downstream distribution module; this module keeps the trust's gross discountable gain and discount component separately identifiable.
* **Sources:**

### <a id="area-au-au-filing"></a>AU filing (5)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-gst-calendar-bas-due-dates-2026-10-10"></a>ATO BAS and annual GST return due dates

* **Rule id:** `au-gst.calendar.bas-due-dates.2026-10-10`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2000 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Monthly BAS is generally due on the 21st of the following month; quarterly BAS is generally due 28 days after quarter end except quarter 2 on 28 February; annual GST returns are due on 31 October or 28 February where no income-tax return is required, subject to next-business-day rollover and agent concessions.
* **Limits and notes:** The agent-program quarterly dates are modelled as data for the 2025-26 and 2026-27 published program years. Annual GST returns that follow the client's income-tax return due date require that due date to be supplied by the caller.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Due dates for lodging and paying your BAS](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/preparing-lodging-and-paying/business-activity-statements-bas/due-dates-for-lodging-and-paying-your-bas) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

  * [ATO | Annual GST reporting](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/lodging-your-bas-or-annual-gst-return/options-for-reporting-and-paying-gst/annual-gst-reporting) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2026 until further notice

* **What the engine applies:** AMITs use the AMIT tax return, MITs and ordinary trusts use a trust tax return, and companies plus public trading trusts use a company tax return.

#### <a id="rule-au-au-returns-due-dates-2026-07-01"></a>Australian income-tax return due dates for June balancers and substituted accounting periods

* **Rule id:** `au-returns.due-dates.2026-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2026 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Self-lodger June balancers are modelled at 31 October. Registered-agent due dates depend on lodgment history, size, tax liability and SAP status, with specific ATO dates for companies and trusts.
* **Limits and notes:** The standard 31 October self-lodger date for June balancers is kept as product policy for this platform. Some ATO programs provide later dates for specific populations; callers should override where a different legislative instrument or deferral applies. This module shows the statutory ATO date only and does not adjust weekends or public holidays to the next business day.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Due dates by topic – income tax](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/preparing-lodging-and-paying/reports-and-returns/due-dates-for-lodging-and-paying/due-dates-by-topic/income-tax) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Registered agent lodgment program – individuals and trusts](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-and-super-professionals/for-tax-professionals/prepare-and-lodge/registered-agent-lodgment-program/due-dates-for-tax-returns-by-client-type/individuals-and-trusts) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Registered agent lodgment program – companies and super funds](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-and-super-professionals/for-tax-professionals/prepare-and-lodge/registered-agent-lodgment-program/due-dates-for-tax-returns-by-client-type/companies-and-super-funds) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Substituted accounting periods](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-and-super-professionals/for-tax-professionals/prepare-and-lodge/registered-agent-lodgment-program/due-dates-for-tax-returns-by-client-type/substituted-accounting-periods) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-dates-income-year-and-sap-dates-2025-07-01"></a>Australian income-year and substituted accounting period date conventions

* **Rule id:** `au-dates.income-year-and-sap-dates.2025-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2025 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** The default Australian income year runs from 1 July to 30 June. For approved substituted accounting periods, trust lodgment is modelled to the last day of the fourth month after year end and company lodgment/payment to the seventh/sixth month milestones.
* **Limits and notes:** ATO registered-agent substituted-accounting-period guidance uses trust lodgment by the last day of the fourth month after year end, company payment by the first day of the sixth month, and company lodgment by the 15th day of the seventh month.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Due dates by topic – income tax](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/preparing-lodging-and-paying/reports-and-returns/due-dates-for-lodging-and-paying/due-dates-by-topic/income-tax) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Substituted accounting periods](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-and-super-professionals/for-tax-professionals/prepare-and-lodge/registered-agent-lodgment-program/due-dates-for-tax-returns-by-client-type/substituted-accounting-periods) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-mit-reporting-due-dates-2026"></a>MIT AIIR and PAYG withholding due dates

* **Rule id:** `au-mit.reporting-due-dates.2026`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2026 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Investment bodies generally lodge the AIIR by 31 October, but MIT fund-payment withholding information is due within 6 months and 14 days after the MIT income year. Small withholders report and pay quarterly on activity statements and medium withholders monthly.
* **Limits and notes:** This helper assumes standard monthly or quarterly activity-statement cycles and does not attempt to model agent concessions or bespoke extension approvals.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Due date for the AIIR](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/preparing-lodging-and-paying/third-party-reporting/annual-investment-income-report/due-date-for-the-aiir) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

### <a id="area-au-au-gst"></a>AU GST (5)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-gst-rate-and-bas-2026-10-10"></a>Australian GST rate and BAS label set

* **Rule id:** `au-gst.rate-and-bas.2026-10-10`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2000 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** GST is 10% on most taxable supplies from 1 July 2000. Current full BAS reporting uses G1, G2, G3, G10, G11, 1A and 1B; Simpler BAS uses G1, 1A and 1B.
* **Limits and notes:** The brief expected a G4 input-taxed BAS label, but the current ATO BAS pages read on 2026-10-10 do not include a current standalone G4 field. The engine therefore keeps G4 only as an internal analytic subtotal. The ATO step pages also allow GST-exclusive G1/G10/G11 amounts under the accounts method if that choice is made; this engine defaults to GST-inclusive BAS amounts unless the caller opts out.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Goods and services tax (GST)](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/preparing-lodging-and-paying/business-activity-statements-bas/goods-and-services-tax-gst) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | GST reporting methods](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/preparing-lodging-and-paying/business-activity-statements-bas/goods-and-services-tax-gst/gst-reporting-methods) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Step 1: Sales](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/completing-your-bas-for-gst/complete-your-bas/step-1-sales) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Step 3: Purchases](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/completing-your-bas-for-gst/complete-your-bas/step-3-purchases) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-gst-accounting-methods-and-time-limit-2026-10-10"></a>Cash basis, non-cash basis and four-year input-tax-credit limit

* **Rule id:** `au-gst.accounting-methods-and-time-limit.2026-10-10`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2000 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Cash-basis GST is attributed when payment is made or received; non-cash GST is attributed when invoice or payment happens first; GST credits generally expire four years after the BAS due date for the first period in which they could have been claimed.
* **Limits and notes:** The engine applies the ATO's $82.50 tax-invoice threshold and four-year claim limit as validation checks; it does not automatically re-open prior BAS periods.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Choosing an accounting method](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/accounting-for-gst-in-your-business/choosing-an-accounting-method) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Time limits on GST credits and refunds](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/claiming-gst-credits/time-limits-on-gst-credits-and-refunds) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Tax invoices](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/tax-invoices) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-gst-registration-and-penalties-2026-10-10"></a>GST registration threshold, FTL penalty units and GIC

* **Rule id:** `au-gst.registration-and-penalties.2026-10-10`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2024 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** GST registration is generally required once current or projected GST turnover reaches $75,000 ($150,000 for non-profits), failure-to-lodge penalties are based on penalty units per 28 days or part thereof, and GIC compounds daily using quarterly ATO rates.
* **Limits and notes:** The penalty helper assumes one penalty-unit value for the penalty event date supplied by the caller. It does not model remission, safe harbour or bespoke compliance discretion.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | How GST registration works](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/registering-for-gst) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Failure to lodge on time penalty](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/paying-the-ato/interest-and-penalties/penalties/failure-to-lodge-on-time-penalty) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Penalty units](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/paying-the-ato/interest-and-penalties/penalties/penalty-units) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | General interest charge](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/paying-the-ato/interest-and-penalties/interest-we-charge/general-interest-charge) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | General interest charge rates](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/general-interest-charge-rates) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-gst-codes-platform-catalogue-2026-10-10"></a>Platform GST code catalogue mapped to BAS labels

* **Rule id:** `au-gst.codes.platform-catalogue.2026-10-10`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2000 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (secondary source only)
* **What the engine applies:** Australia does not publish a single official ledger tax-code list comparable to Singapore's ASR+ codes, so the engine uses a platform catalogue that maps common property-industry transactions cleanly to current BAS labels and GST-credit outcomes.
* **Limits and notes:** Current ATO guidance supports the BAS labels and the broad GST classes used here, but Australia does not publish an official ledger-code catalogue and the exact row set, claimability flags, reverse-charge placeholder, and G4 analytic subtotal are platform constructs. #### <a id="rule-au-au-gst-property-2026-10-10"></a>Property classification, margin scheme, GST at settlement and Division 129

* **Rule id:** `au-gst.property.2026-10-10`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2000 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (secondary source only)
* **What the engine applies:** Commercial leases and sales are generally taxable, residential rent and existing residential premises are generally input taxed, new residential premises are generally taxable, and GST at settlement usually requires purchaser withholding on new residential premises and some potential residential land.

### <a id="area-au-au-identifiers"></a>AU identifiers (4)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-members-tfn-abn-withholding-2017-plus"></a>Resident TFN or ABN withholding for unit trust and AMIT payments

* **Rule id:** `au-members.tfn-abn-withholding.2017-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2017 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Investment bodies, including unit trusts and MITs, withhold from resident investment income when the investor has not quoted a TFN or ABN or claimed an exemption. The engine uses the top resident individual rate including Medicare levy, and does not withhold where the payment is only tax-deferred capital.
* **Limits and notes:** The ATO guidance states that the investment body withholds at the top rate of tax, the Medicare-levy note still applies, and the AMMA/SDS guide points to sections 12-140 and 12-145 of Schedule 1 to the TAA 1953.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Withholding from investment income](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/payg-withholding/payments-you-need-to-withhold-from/withholding-from-investment-income) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Tax rates for Australian residents](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-australian-residents) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | AMMA statement and SDS 2024 guidance notes](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/attribution-managed-investment-trust-member-annual-statement-standard-distribution-statement-2024/guidance-notes) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-identifiers-abn-2026-10-10"></a>ABN format and checksum

* **Rule id:** `au-identifiers.abn.2026-10-10`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2000 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (secondary source only)
* **What the engine applies:** ABNs are 11 digits; the public ABR validation approach uses the published weighting table and a modulus-89 test after subtracting 1 from the first digit.
* **Limits and notes:** The ABR Help page was reachable only as a scheduled-maintenance notice on 2026-10-10, so the checksum table is treated as verified secondary rather than fully re-verified from the live ABR help text on that date.
* **Sources:**
  * [ABN Lookup | Format of the ABN](https://abr.business.gov.au/Help/AbnFormat?SearchText=51824753556) (ABR, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ABN Lookup | Web services](https://abr.business.gov.au/Tools/WebServices) (ABR, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-identifiers-acn-2026-10-10"></a>ACN format, relationship to company ABNs, and checksum

* **Rule id:** `au-identifiers.acn.2026-10-10`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2000 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Assumption (needs a reviewer's judgement)
* **What the engine applies:** ACNs are 9 digits and many company ABNs embed the ACN as their final 9 digits; the engine validates ACNs using the standard weighted check-digit method and only derives an ACN from an ABN when the derived 9 digits also pass ACN validation.
* **Limits and notes:** A live ASIC checksum specification could not be re-opened from the public site in this environment on 2026-10-10. The ACN checksum implementation is therefore a platform assumption aligned to the standard market formula and checked against published specimen numbers.
* **Sources:**
  * [ABN Lookup | Web services](https://abr.business.gov.au/Tools/WebServices) (ABR, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Tax invoices](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/gst-excise-and-indirect-taxes/gst/tax-invoices) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-identifiers-tfn-2026-10-10"></a>TFN privacy handling and checksum validation

* **Rule id:** `au-identifiers.tfn.2026-10-10`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2000 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Assumption (needs a reviewer's judgement)
* **What the engine applies:** The engine validates 8-digit and 9-digit TFNs using the standard modulus-11 weighting approach, rejects ATO payer-code placeholders, and never echoes a full TFN back to callers.
* **Limits and notes:** The ATO pages retrieved on 2026-10-10 clearly confirm TFN sensitivity and payer-code placeholders but do not publish a checksum specification in the fetched public material, so the checksum algorithm remains an assumption that must not be treated as authoritative identity evidence.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Tax file number and withholding declarations](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/payg-withholding/payments-you-need-to-withhold-from/payments-to-employees/tax-file-number-and-withholding-declarations) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Paper TFN declaration form for payees](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/tfn-declaration/paper-tfn-declaration-form-for-payees) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Lodging tax file number (TFN) declaration data online](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/tfn-declaration-lodging-online) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

### <a id="area-au-au-income-tax"></a>AU income tax (3)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-company-tax-rate-and-bre-2017-07-01"></a>Australian company tax rate and base rate entity test

* **Rule id:** `au-company-tax.rate-and-bre.2017-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2017 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** From 2017–18 onward, the lower company tax rate changed by income year: 27.5% at sub-$25 million turnover for 2017–18, 27.5% at sub-$50 million turnover for 2018–19 and 2019–20, 26% for 2020–21, and 25% from 2021–22 onward. Non-base-rate entities stay at 30%.
* **Limits and notes:** This module keeps amounts in cents for engine precision. Franking credits, offsets, instalment credits and company-loss ownership tracing are flagged but not fully modelled.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Company tax rates – 2025–26](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/company-tax-rates/tax-rates-2025-26) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Company tax rate changes](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/company-tax-rate-changes) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Lower company tax rate](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/corporate-tax-measures-and-assurance/privately-owned-and-wealthy-groups/what-attracts-our-attention/business-structure/lower-company-tax-rate) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-company-tax-loss-review-2026-07-01"></a>Company loss usage needs continuity of ownership or business continuity support

* **Rule id:** `au-company-tax.loss-review.2026-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2026 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** The losses schedule instructions require companies to consider the continuity of majority ownership test and, if failed, the business continuity test before deducting prior-year losses.
* **Limits and notes:** The engine only consumes caller-supplied pass/fail facts for the ownership and business continuity tests; it does not determine them from share registers.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Losses schedule 2026 instructions – Part B ownership and business continuity test](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/losses-schedule-2026-instructions/instructions-to-complete-the-losses-schedule-2026/part-b-ownership-and-business-continuity-test) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-mapping-property-ledger-dictionary-2026-10-10"></a>Australian property-industry chart-of-accounts mapping dictionary

* **Rule id:** `au-mapping.property-ledger-dictionary.2026-10-10`
* **Effective:** from 10 Oct 2026 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Assumption (needs a reviewer's judgement)
* **What the engine applies:** The AU mapper classifies accounts as profit and loss or balance sheet using explicit wording cues first, then applies Australian property-tax category rules and only falls back to hints or prefixes with low confidence.
* **Limits and notes:** The account-caption dictionary is product policy informed by Australian property ledgers (Yardi, MRI, Xero, MYOB and SAP style names). Unknown captions must stay low confidence at 0.30 or below.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Company tax rate changes](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/company-tax-rate-changes) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Trust tax return 2025 instructions – general information for trusts](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/trust-tax-return-2025-instructions/general-information-for-trusts) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

### <a id="area-au-au-land-tax"></a>AU land tax (18)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-act-foreign-2018-07-01"></a>ACT foreign ownership surcharge for land tax

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.act.foreign.2018-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2018 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Foreign persons who own residential land in the ACT pay a land tax surcharge of 0.75% of the Average Unimproved Value per year from 1 July 2018, in addition to land tax.
* **Sources:**
  * [ACT Revenue Office | Foreign ownership surcharge for land tax](https://www.revenue.act.gov.au/rates-and-property-charges/land-tax/foreign-ownership-surcharge-for-land-tax) (ACT Revenue Office, read 19 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-act-commercial-nil"></a>ACT land tax does not apply to commercial properties

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.act.commercial.nil`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2025 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** The ACT Revenue Office says land tax does not apply to commercial properties. The engine returns a cited nil for ACT holdings not marked as residential.
* **Sources:**
  * [ACT Revenue Office | About land tax](https://www.revenue.act.gov.au/rates-and-property-charges/land-tax/about-land-tax) (ACT Revenue Office, read 19 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-act-residential-2025-07-01"></a>ACT land tax on residential property (2025-26)

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.act.residential.2025-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2025 to 30 Jun 2026
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** For 2025-26 the ACT land tax fixed charge is A$1,693 and the valuation rates run from 0.54% to 1.26% of AUV, the same rates as 2026-27. The foreign ownership surcharge stays at 0.75% of AUV.
* **Limits and notes:** The determination commenced on 1 July 2025 (land-tax year 2026 in this app). The engine annualises the charge and does not reproduce quarterly day-count percentages.
* **Sources:**
  * [Taxation Administration (Amounts Payable—Land Tax) Determination 2025 (DI2025-153)](https://www.legislation.act.gov.au/di/2025-153/) (ACT Legislation Register, read 19 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-act-residential-2026-07-01"></a>ACT land tax on residential property (2026-27)

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.act.residential.2026-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2026 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** ACT land tax applies to residential properties that are not a principal place of residence, including rented or vacant properties and properties owned by a corporation or trustee. From 1 July 2026 the annual fixed charge is A$1,778 plus valuation rates from 0.54% to 1.26% of AUV.
* **Limits and notes:** The engine annualises the 2026-27 fixed charge and valuation schedule (land-tax year 2027 in this app) and does not reproduce quarterly day-count percentages.
* **Sources:**
  * [ACT Revenue Office | About land tax](https://www.revenue.act.gov.au/rates-and-property-charges/land-tax/about-land-tax) (ACT Revenue Office, read 19 Oct 2026)
  * [ACT Revenue Office | How land tax is calculated](https://www.revenue.act.gov.au/rates-and-property-charges/land-tax/how-land-tax-is-calculated) (ACT Revenue Office, read 19 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-nsw-general-2024-01-01"></a>NSW land tax thresholds and rates

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.nsw.general.2024-01-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** NSW general land tax applies above the indexed threshold with A$100 plus 1.6% up to the premium threshold and 2% above it. Thresholds are A$1.075m / A$6.571m from 2024 onwards and fixed after the 2024-25 Budget.
* **Sources:**
  * [Revenue NSW | Land tax thresholds and rates](https://www.revenue.nsw.gov.au/taxes-duties-levies-royalties/land-tax/understanding-land-tax/thresholds-and-rates) (Revenue NSW, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [Revenue NSW | How individuals and joint owners are assessed for land tax](https://www.revenue.nsw.gov.au/taxes-duties-levies-royalties/land-tax/understanding-land-tax/types-of-landowners/individuals-and-joint-owners) (Revenue NSW, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-nsw-special-trust-current"></a>NSW special-trust land tax

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.nsw.special-trust.current`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Special or discretionary trusts do not receive the tax-free threshold in NSW and are taxed at 1.6% up to the premium threshold and 2% thereafter.
* **Sources:**
  * [Revenue NSW | How trusts are assessed for land tax](https://www.revenue.nsw.gov.au/taxes-duties-levies-royalties/land-tax/understanding-land-tax/types-of-landowners/trusts) (Revenue NSW, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-nsw-surcharge-2025-01-01"></a>NSW surcharge land tax for foreign owners

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.nsw.surcharge.2025-01-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** NSW surcharge land tax applies to residential land owned by foreign persons at 5% from 2025, 4% for 2023-24 and 2% for 2018-22, with no tax-free threshold.
* **Sources:**
  * [Revenue NSW | What is surcharge land tax](https://www.revenue.nsw.gov.au/taxes-duties-levies-royalties/land-tax/surcharge-land-tax/what-is-surcharge-land-tax) (Revenue NSW, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [Revenue NSW | How companies are assessed for land tax](https://www.revenue.nsw.gov.au/taxes-duties-levies-royalties/land-tax/understanding-land-tax/types-of-landowners/companies) (Revenue NSW, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-qld-current"></a>Queensland land tax for individuals, companies and trusts

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.qld.current`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Queensland land tax is assessed on freehold land owned at midnight on 30 June. Individuals use a A$600,000 threshold; companies and trustees use A$350,000; foreign companies, foreign trusts and absentee individuals pay an additional 3% surcharge above A$350,000.
* **Sources:**
  * [Queensland Revenue Office | Land tax threshold and rates for individuals](https://qro.qld.gov.au/land-tax/calculate/individual/) (Queensland Revenue Office, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [Queensland Revenue Office | Land tax threshold and rates for companies and trusts](https://qro.qld.gov.au/land-tax/calculate/company-trust/) (Queensland Revenue Office, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [Queensland Revenue Office | Land tax threshold and rates for foreign companies and trusts](https://qro.qld.gov.au/land-tax/calculate/foreign-company-trust/) (Queensland Revenue Office, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [Queensland Revenue Office | Land tax threshold and rates for absentees](https://qro.qld.gov.au/land-tax/calculate/absentee/) (Queensland Revenue Office, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-sa-general"></a>South Australia land tax general rates

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.sa.general`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2021 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** South Australian general land tax is nil up to the indexed threshold (A$833,000 for 2025-26, A$936,000 for 2026-27), then 50 cents, A$1.00, A$2.00 and A$2.40 for every A$100 or part above each step. Applies to owners other than trusts and to trusts assessed at the general rates, such as listed or widely held public unit trust schemes.
* **Limits and notes:** Each financial year's table is held from 2021-22 to 2026-27. No assessment is issued when the calculated tax is under A$20. Exemptions (principal place of residence, primary production) are out of scope.
* **Sources:**
  * [RevenueSA | Land tax rates and thresholds (2020-21 to 2026-27 general rates)](https://revenuesa.sa.gov.au/landtax/rates-and-thresholds) (RevenueSA, read 19 Oct 2026)
  * [RevenueSA | Trust types not subject to the trust land tax rates](https://revenuesa.sa.gov.au/landtax/calculate-land-tax/trust-types-not-subject-to-the-trust-land-tax-rates) (RevenueSA, read 19 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-sa-trust"></a>South Australia land tax trust rates

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.sa.trust`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2021 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Land held on trust is taxed at the trust rates from A$25,000 (A$125 plus 50 cents for every A$100 or part above A$25,000, rising to A$2.40) unless the trust is assessed at the general rates, for example an excluded trust or a fixed or unit trust whose beneficiaries or unitholders have been notified to RevenueSA.
* **Limits and notes:** Whether a trust is assessed at the general rates depends on notifications to RevenueSA; the app's Trust surcharge applies setting stands in for that decision.
* **Sources:**
  * [RevenueSA | Land tax rates and thresholds (2020-21 to 2026-27 trust rates)](https://revenuesa.sa.gov.au/landtax/rates-and-thresholds) (RevenueSA, read 19 Oct 2026)
  * [RevenueSA | Land held on trust](https://revenuesa.sa.gov.au/landtax/land-held-on-trust) (RevenueSA, read 19 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-tas-foreign-2025-07-01"></a>Tasmania foreign investor land tax surcharge

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.tas.foreign.2025-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2025 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Tasmania charges FILTS at 2% of the assessed land value of the foreign-owned portion of General Land acquired on or after 1 July 2022, in addition to ordinary land tax and even below the ordinary land-tax threshold.
* **Limits and notes:** The current ordinary land-tax table is effective from 1 July 2025; the surcharge source states the underlying FILTS liability applies to relevant property acquired on or after 1 July 2022.
* **Sources:**
  * [State Revenue Office Tasmania | Rate of surcharge](https://www.sro.tas.gov.au/land-tax/foreign-investor-land-tax-surcharge/rate-of-surcharge) (State Revenue Office Tasmania, read 19 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-tas-general-2025-07-01"></a>Tasmania land tax general rates

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.tas.general.2025-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2025 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Tasmanian land tax on General Land is nil below A$125,000 from 1 July 2025, then A$50 plus 0.45% above A$125,000, and A$1,737.50 plus 1.5% above A$500,000.
* **Limits and notes:** The engine applies the General Land scale and aggregates holdings by owner. Principal residence, primary-production and exempt-land classifications are out of scope.
* **Sources:**
  * [State Revenue Office Tasmania | Rates of land tax](https://www.sro.tas.gov.au/land-tax/rates-of-land-tax) (State Revenue Office Tasmania, read 19 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-vic-general-2022-01-01"></a>Victoria historical land tax rates for 2022-23

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.vic.general.2022-01-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 to 31 Dec 2023

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.vic.general.2024-01-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2024 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-vic-trust-current"></a>Victoria trust surcharge and absentee owner surcharge

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.vic.trust.current`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Most Victorian trusts use the trust surcharge scale from A$25,000, unless a notified trust falls back to general rates. The absentee owner surcharge is 4% from the 2024 land-tax year and 2% for 2020-2023, applied on top of the base rates.

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-wa-mrit-current"></a>WA Metropolitan Region Improvement Tax

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.wa.mrit.current`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Land in the Perth metropolitan region also pays the Metropolitan Region Improvement Tax: 0.14% of the aggregated taxable value above A$300,000, assessed with land tax.
* **Limits and notes:** Holdings are treated as metropolitan unless the caller marks them otherwise. Each WA property profile in the app has an In Perth metropolitan region flag; profiles saved before the flag existed count as metropolitan, so check the flag for any WA property outside the region.
* **Sources:**
  * [WA Department of Treasury and Finance | Land tax assessment (MRIT rates)](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/department-of-treasury-and-finance/land-tax-assessment) (Department of Treasury and Finance, Western Australia, read 19 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-wa-general-current"></a>Western Australia land tax scale

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.wa.general.current`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Western Australia charges land tax on the aggregated taxable value above A$300,000: A$300 up to A$420,000, then A$300 plus 0.25%, A$1,750 plus 0.9%, A$8,950 plus 1.8%, A$66,550 plus 2% and, above A$11,000,000, A$186,550 plus 2.67% of the excess. Trustees are assessed as owners; there is no trust or foreign-owner surcharge.
* **Limits and notes:** The page gives the current scale and refers to the Land Tax Act 2002 for earlier years. Secondary sources describe the scale as unchanged since 2018-19, so it is applied from the engine's earliest assessment year (2022).
* **Sources:**
  * [WA Department of Treasury and Finance | Land tax assessment (land tax rates)](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/department-of-treasury-and-finance/land-tax-assessment) (Department of Treasury and Finance, Western Australia, read 19 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-land-tax-nt-nil"></a>Northern Territory has no annual land tax

* **Rule id:** `au-land-tax.nt.nil`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (secondary source only)
* **What the engine applies:** The Northern Territory Revenue Office publishes stamp duty and other Territory taxes, but no annual land tax regime; the engine returns a cited nil for NT land tax.
* **Limits and notes:** This is a cited nil by official-scope exclusion: the Territory Revenue Office property-tax material covers stamp duty, not annual land tax. No NT land-tax legislation or rate table is published by the Territory Revenue Office.
* **Sources:**
  * [NT Department of Treasury and Finance | Stamp duty](https://treasury.nt.gov.au/dtf/territory-revenue-office/stamp-duty) (Department of Treasury and Finance, Northern Territory, read 19 Oct 2026)

### <a id="area-au-au-mit"></a>AU MIT / AMIT (2)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-mit-fund-payment-definition-and-notice-2016-plus"></a>MIT fund payments, notices and payment statements

* **Rule id:** `au-mit.fund-payment-definition-and-notice.2016-plus`
* **Effective:** from 5 May 2016 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Fund payments broadly comprise Australian-source MIT net income excluding dividends, interest, royalties, foreign-source amounts and gains on non-taxable Australian property. MITs and intermediaries must withhold, or otherwise notify and disclose the relevant amount at or before payment, and website disclosures must remain available for 5 continuous years.
* **Limits and notes:** The engine outputs structured notice content rather than a PDF. Payment summaries are modelled as statement data, not ATO-prescribed forms, because the ATO says the format is not prescribed provided the minimum fields are present.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Withholding tax arrangements for managed investment trust fund payments](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/international-tax-for-business/in-detail/investing-in-australia/withholding-tax-arrangements-for-managed-investment-trust-fund-payments) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Withholding on fund payments for MITs](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/trusts/specific-rules-for-some-trusts/managed-investment-trusts/managed-investment-trusts-overview/withholding-rules/withholding-on-fund-payments-for-mits) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Withholding for MITs](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/trusts/specific-rules-for-some-trusts/managed-investment-trusts/managed-investment-trusts-overview/withholding-rules/withholding-for-mits) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-members-mit-foreign-member-withholding-2008-plus"></a>MIT withholding rates by foreign member status and fund-payment category

* **Rule id:** `au-members.mit-foreign-member-withholding.2008-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2008 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Foreign residents in information-exchange countries generally face 15% MIT withholding on ordinary fund payments, 30% outside those countries, 10% for eligible clean building MIT payments, 30% for NCMI, and 15% for eligible build-to-rent fund payments from 1 January 2025.
* **Limits and notes:** The 2024 AMMA/SDS guide confirms a 30% withholding rate where a disclosed amount is NCMI. Foreign pension and sovereign classes are treated conservatively as ordinary foreign funds for fund-payment withholding because no separate ATO rate concession for fund payments was verified on the retrieval date.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Withholding tax arrangements for managed investment trust fund payments](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/international-tax-for-business/in-detail/investing-in-australia/withholding-tax-arrangements-for-managed-investment-trust-fund-payments) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Withholding on fund payments for MITs](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/trusts/specific-rules-for-some-trusts/managed-investment-trusts/managed-investment-trusts-overview/withholding-rules/withholding-on-fund-payments-for-mits) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Build to rent development tax incentives](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/assets-and-property/build-to-rent-development-tax-incentives) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [Federal Register of Legislation | Taxation Administration Amendment (Updating the List of Exchange of Information Countries) Regulations 2018](https://www.legislation.gov.au/Details/F2018L01596) (Federal Register of Legislation, read 10 Oct 2026)

* **Rule id:** `au-transfer-duty.act.foreign.nil`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2022 until further notice

* **Rule id:** `au-transfer-duty.act.residential.2022-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-transfer-duty-nt-foreign-nil"></a>Northern Territory has no foreign purchaser duty surcharge

* **Rule id:** `au-transfer-duty.nt.foreign.nil`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-transfer-duty-nt-general-2022-07-01"></a>Northern Territory stamp duty on land

* **Rule id:** `au-transfer-duty.nt.general.2022-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** NT stamp duty on land uses the V-squared formula up to A$525,000, then 4.95% above A$525,000 and below A$3m, 5.75% from A$3m and below A$5m, and 5.95% from A$5m.

#### <a id="rule-au-au-transfer-duty-nsw-historical-2022-07-01"></a>NSW indexed transfer-duty schedules from 1 July 2022 to 30 June 2026

* **Rule id:** `au-transfer-duty.nsw.historical.2022-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2022 to 30 Jun 2026
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Revenue NSW publishes indexed duty and premium thresholds for each financial year. The engine includes the 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 schedules so historical recomputations stay aligned to the contract date.
* **Sources:**
  * [Revenue NSW | Past thresholds and rates for transfer duty](https://www.revenue.nsw.gov.au/taxes-duties-levies-royalties/transfer-duty/understanding-transfer-duty/calculate-transfer-duty/past-thresholds-and-rates) (Revenue NSW, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-transfer-duty-nsw-landholder-2024-02-01"></a>NSW landholder duty

* **Rule id:** `au-transfer-duty.nsw.landholder.2024-02-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2023 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** NSW landholder duty applies once a landholder has NSW landholdings of A$2m or more (Duties Act 1997 (NSW) s 146); below that there is no landholder duty. From 1 February 2024 most private unit trusts use a 20% significant-interest threshold; private companies and registered wholesale or imminent wholesale unit trusts use 50%; public landholders use 90%.
* **Limits and notes:** The engine models current direct single-step relevant acquisitions. Pre-1 July 2023 public-landholder calculations and multi-step statement-period histories require manual review.
* **Sources:**
  * [Revenue NSW | What is landholder duty](https://www.revenue.nsw.gov.au/taxes-duties-levies-royalties/transfer-duty/landholder-duty/what-is-landholder-duty) (Revenue NSW, read 10 Oct 2026)

* **Rule id:** `au-transfer-duty.qld.afad.2016-10-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Oct 2016 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Queensland AFAD is 8% for relevant transfer-duty, landholder-duty and corporate-trustee-duty acquisitions of AFAD residential land by foreign individuals, foreign corporations and trustees of foreign trusts.

#### <a id="rule-au-au-transfer-duty-qld-landholder-current"></a>Queensland landholder duty

* **Rule id:** `au-transfer-duty.qld.landholder.current`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2011 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Queensland landholder duty applies once a corporation or listed unit trust has Queensland landholdings of A$2m or more. Relevant acquisitions are generally 50% for private landholders and 90% for public landholders. Public landholder duty is 10% of the transfer duty on all Queensland landholdings. Units in an unlisted unit trust are trust interests instead: any acquisition is a trust acquisition, charged transfer duty on the higher of the consideration and the acquired share of the trust's dutiable property, with no value or interest threshold.
* **Limits and notes:** For a trust acquisition the engine uses the acquired share of the land value; it has no consideration input, so a reviewer must check the consideration is not higher. Unlisted wholesale unit trusts are not modelled.
* **Sources:**
  * [Queensland Revenue Office | Landholders and land-holdings for landholder duty](https://qro.qld.gov.au/duties/investors/landholder/landholders/) (Queensland Revenue Office, read 19 Oct 2026)
  * [Queensland Revenue Office | Relevant acquisitions in a landholder](https://qro.qld.gov.au/duties/investors/landholder/relevant-acquisitions/) (Queensland Revenue Office, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [Queensland Revenue Office | Calculating landholder duty](https://qro.qld.gov.au/duties/investors/landholder/calculating/) (Queensland Revenue Office, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [Queensland Revenue Office | Additional foreign acquirer duty for landholder duty](https://qro.qld.gov.au/duties/investors/landholder/afad/) (Queensland Revenue Office, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [Queensland Revenue Office | Trust interest, acquisitions and surrenders (worked example: a 20% interest in a trust holding A$1m of land has a dutiable value of A$200,000)](https://qro.qld.gov.au/duties/investors/trusts/interest-acquisitions/) (Queensland Revenue Office, read 19 Oct 2026)

* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Queensland uses a nil band up to A$5,000 and then A$1.50, A$3.50, A$4.50 and A$5.75 for each A$100 or part of A$100 above the threshold, with the current schedule applying to transfer duty, corporate trustee duty and landholder duty.
* **Sources:**

* **Rule id:** `au-transfer-duty.sa.landholder.2018-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2018 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** SA landholder duty applies when a prescribed interest is acquired or increased in an entity that holds residential or primary-production land. Prescribed interests are 50% for private companies and private unit trusts, and 90% for listed companies and public unit trusts; entities holding only qualifying land are outside duty from 1 July 2018.

#### <a id="rule-au-au-transfer-duty-sa-qualifying-land-phaseout-2015-12-07"></a>South Australia qualifying-land duty phase-out

* **Rule id:** `au-transfer-duty.sa.qualifying-land.phaseout.2015-12-07`
* **Effective:** from 7 Dec 2015 to 30 Jun 2018
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** For qualifying land, SA allowed no reduction for contracts on or before 6 December 2015, a one-third reduction from 7 December 2015 to 30 June 2017, a two-thirds reduction from 1 July 2017 to 30 June 2018, and a full reduction from 1 July 2018.
* **Limits and notes:** The same phase-out is applied to notional acquisitions under Part 4 because IC 103 treats conveyances and transfers as including notional acquisitions of underlying local land assets.
* **Sources:**
  * [RevenueSA | Information Circular 103: stamp duty on qualifying land](https://www.revenuesa.sa.gov.au/tools-and-resources/resources/publications/information-circulars/information-circulars/ic_103/ic_103_07122018) (RevenueSA, read 19 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-transfer-duty-sa-qualifying-land-2018-07-01"></a>South Australia: no duty on qualifying (non-residential) land

* **Rule id:** `au-transfer-duty.sa.qualifying-land.2018-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2018 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** No stamp duty applies to a conveyance of non-residential, non-primary-production land (qualifying land) under a contract entered into on or after 1 July 2018. A mixed purchase is charged the residential share of the duty on the whole value, to the nearest cent, as in RevenueSA's worked example.
* **Limits and notes:** Stamp Duties Act 1923 s105A / former s71DC. Whether land is qualifying land follows the property kind in the profile.
* **Sources:**
  * [RevenueSA | Information Circular 103: stamp duty on qualifying land](https://www.revenuesa.sa.gov.au/resources/publications/information-circulars/information-circulars/ic_103/information-circular-103_21112022) (RevenueSA, read 19 Oct 2026)

* **Rule id:** `au-transfer-duty.vic.landholder.current`

* **What the engine applies:** Victoria treats a company or unit trust with Victorian landholdings of A$1m or more as a landholder; below A$1m there is no landholder duty, and between A$1m and A$2m duty is phased in (Duties Act 2000 (Vic) s 89). Significant-interest thresholds are 20% for private unit trusts, 50% for private companies and wholesale unit trusts, and 90% for public landholders. Public landholders pay 10% of the duty that would apply to a transfer of all Victorian landholdings.

#### <a id="rule-au-au-transfer-duty-wa-landholder-2008-07-01"></a>Western Australia landholder duty

* **Rule id:** `au-transfer-duty.wa.landholder.2008-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2008 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** WA landholder duty applies to corporations and unit trust schemes with WA land assets of A$2m or more. A significant interest is 50% in an unlisted landholder and 90% in a listed landholder. Duty is charged at the general rate on the acquirer's share of the landholder's WA land assets; listed landholders get no concession.
