### <a id="area-au-au-trust-tax"></a>AU trust taxation (7)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-amit-trust-components-and-attribution-2016-plus"></a>AMIT trust components, fair-and-reasonable attribution and character retention

* **Rule id:** `au-amit.trust-components-and-attribution.2016-plus`
* **Effective:** from 5 May 2016 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** An AMIT first determines trust components by character, then attributes them to members on a fair and reasonable basis. Character and tax offsets flow through to members, who are treated as if they derived or received the amounts directly.
* **Limits and notes:** The engine accepts already-classified component inputs from the trust tax computation and applies discovery-year adjustments and rounding by character rather than recomputing taxable income from ledger detail.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Calculating AMIT income trust components](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/trusts/specific-rules-for-some-trusts/managed-investment-trusts/managed-investment-trusts-overview/attribution-managed-investment-trusts/attribution-method-for-managed-investment-trusts/calculating-amit-income-trust-components) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Attributing amounts to members](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/trusts/specific-rules-for-some-trusts/managed-investment-trusts/managed-investment-trusts-overview/attribution-managed-investment-trusts/attribution-method-for-managed-investment-trusts/attributing-amounts-to-members) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Character flow through for AMITs](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/trusts/specific-rules-for-some-trusts/managed-investment-trusts/managed-investment-trusts-overview/attribution-managed-investment-trusts/attribution-method-for-managed-investment-trusts/character-flow-through-for-amits) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-amit-unders-overs-and-cbna-2016-plus"></a>AMIT unders and overs, annual cost base adjustments and AMMA timing

* **Rule id:** `au-amit.unders-overs-and-cbna.2016-plus`
* **Effective:** from 5 May 2016 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Unders and overs can be adjusted in the discovery year or by reissuing the base-year AMMA and AIIR. The AMIT cost base net amount increases cost base where attributed assessable and NANE amounts exceed cash and offsets, and decreases it in the opposite case, with CGT event E10 once cost base is exhausted.
* **Limits and notes:** The engine exposes both the discovery-year adjustment path and the AMMA reissue timing, but does not prepare amended AIIR data files; it returns structured statement content instead.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Unders and overs for AMITs](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/trusts/specific-rules-for-some-trusts/managed-investment-trusts/managed-investment-trusts-overview/attribution-managed-investment-trusts/unders-and-overs-for-amits) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Cost base adjustments for AMIT members](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/trusts/specific-rules-for-some-trusts/managed-investment-trusts/managed-investment-trusts-overview/attribution-managed-investment-trusts/attribution-method-for-managed-investment-trusts/cost-base-adjustments-for-amit-members) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | AMIT reporting requirements](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/trusts/specific-rules-for-some-trusts/managed-investment-trusts/managed-investment-trusts-overview/attribution-managed-investment-trusts/amit-reporting-requirements) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | AMMA statement and SDS 2024 about the AMMA statement and SDS](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/attribution-managed-investment-trust-member-annual-statement-standard-distribution-statement-2024/about-the-amma-statement-and-sds) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-members-general-foreign-trust-tax-2016-plus"></a>Foreign residents outside the MIT withholding regime

* **Rule id:** `au-members.general-foreign-trust-tax.2016-plus`
* **Effective:** from 5 May 2016 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Where a trust is not a withholding MIT, foreign-resident amounts are generally taxed through trustee assessment and statement credits rather than MIT cash withholding. Non-withholding AMITs use the trustee taxation and statement-of-attribution rules.
* **Limits and notes:** This module returns a trustee-assessed scenario with no cash withholding where the payment is outside the withholding-MIT rules.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Withholding for MITs](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/trusts/specific-rules-for-some-trusts/managed-investment-trusts/managed-investment-trusts-overview/withholding-rules/withholding-for-mits) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | AMIT trustee taxation](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/trusts/specific-rules-for-some-trusts/managed-investment-trusts/managed-investment-trusts-overview/attribution-managed-investment-trusts/amit-trustee-taxation) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-trust-tax-statement-of-taxable-income-2022-07-01"></a>Property-trust statement of taxable income

* **Rule id:** `au-trust-tax.statement-of-taxable-income.2022-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Trust net income is worked out under section 95 as if the trustee were a resident taxpayer, replacing accounting capital and timing items with the tax result and adding CGT, Division 40, Division 43 and borrowing-expense schedules.
* **Limits and notes:** The STI engine assumes the CGT schedule has already netted capital losses before passing discountable and other net capital gains into this module.
* **Sources:**
  * [ITAA 1936 section 95](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=PAC/19360027/95) (ATO legal database, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | CGT discount](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/capital-gains-tax/cgt-discount) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Trust tax return 2025 instructions – general information for trusts](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/trust-tax-return-2025-instructions/general-information-for-trusts) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-trust-tax-trust-loss-review-2022-07-01"></a>Trust losses and Division 6C require manual review

* **Rule id:** `au-trust-tax.trust-loss-review.2022-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Trust loss recoupment depends on Schedule 2F tests that vary by trust type, while public trading trusts under Division 6C are taxed like companies and must not stay in the trust STI workflow.
* **Limits and notes:** Division 6C status, trust loss tests and MIT/AMIT distribution mechanics are flagged for review or handled in other AU agents, not fully determined in this module.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Trust loss provisions – about trust loss provisions](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/trusts/trust-income-losses-and-capital-gains/trust-loss-provisions/about-trust-loss-provisions) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Trust loss provisions – which tests to apply](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/trusts/trust-income-losses-and-capital-gains/trust-loss-provisions/which-tests-to-apply) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Attribution MIT tax return instructions 2026 – how to lodge your AMIT tax return and pay](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/attribution-managed-investment-trust-tax-return-instructions-2026/how-to-lodge-your-amit-tax-return-and-pay) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-distribution-cash-policy-and-member-allocation-2026"></a>AU trust distribution policy, member allocation and statements

* **Rule id:** `au-distribution.cash-policy-and-member-allocation.2026`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2026 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Assumption (needs a reviewer's judgement)
* **What the engine applies:** The engine converts accounting distributable income and the trust's distribution policy into declared cash distributions, allocates those distributions and attributed components by deterministic largest-remainder cents, applies optional time-weighted AMIT attribution, and builds AMMA or non-AMIT statement data with withholding reconciliation.
* **Limits and notes:** The ATO materials retrieved for this engine clearly support fair-and-reasonable attribution and show record-date style outcomes, but they did not expressly endorse a daily time-weighted method. The TIME_WEIGHTED_DAILY option is therefore an engine assumption for scenario modelling, while RECORD_DATE remains available.
* **Sources:**
  * [ATO | Attributing amounts to members](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/trusts/specific-rules-for-some-trusts/managed-investment-trusts/managed-investment-trusts-overview/attribution-managed-investment-trusts/attribution-method-for-managed-investment-trusts/attributing-amounts-to-members) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | AMMA statement and SDS 2024 example](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/attribution-managed-investment-trust-member-annual-statement-standard-distribution-statement-2024/amma-statement-or-sds-example) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | AMMA statement and SDS 2024 guidance notes](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/attribution-managed-investment-trust-member-annual-statement-standard-distribution-statement-2024/guidance-notes) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-au-au-trust-tax-trustee-assessment-2022-07-01"></a>Trustee-level tax where no beneficiary is presently entitled or foreign residents are assessed through the trustee

* **Rule id:** `au-trust-tax.trustee-assessment.2022-07-01`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jul 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Assumption (needs a reviewer's judgement)
* **What the engine applies:** Section 99 and section 99A deal with income to which no beneficiary is presently entitled. Section 98 can assess a trustee on behalf of certain beneficiaries, including foreign residents. This engine only verifies foreign-resident individual rate modelling and flags the rest for review.
* **Limits and notes:** Sections 99, 99A and 251S were read directly, and the 2% Medicare levy rate was read from the ATO resident-rates page. The section 99A special-rate percentage is still modelled to the top published resident marginal rate in the cited sources, so the overall rule remains an assumption. Beneficiary classes other than foreign-resident individuals are not modelled.
* **Sources:**
  * [ITAA 1936 section 99](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=PAC/19360027/99) (ATO legal database, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ITAA 1936 section 99A](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=PAC/19360027/99A) (ATO legal database, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Foreign resident tax rates](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-foreign-residents) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ATO | Australian resident tax rates](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-australian-residents) (ATO, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ITAA 1936 section 100A](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=PAC/19360027/100A) (ATO legal database, read 10 Oct 2026)
  * [ITAA 1936 section 251S](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=PAC/19360027/251S) (ATO legal database, read 10 Oct 2026)

## Singapore

### <a id="area-sg-capital-allowances"></a>Capital allowances (3)

#### <a id="rule-sg-capital-allowances-iba-lia-s19b-2022-plus"></a>IBA, LIA and section 19B

* **Rule id:** `capital-allowances.iba-lia-s19b.2022-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** IBA is phased out except for transitional cases. LIA remains available for approved projects, and section 19B writing-down allowances continue for qualifying IPR acquisitions up to the last day of the basis period for YA 2028.
* **Limits and notes:** The module models only the core mechanical rules and not approval workflows or EIS cash-conversion elections.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Industrial Building Allowance (IBA)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/income-deductions-for-companies/claiming-allowances/industrial-building-allowance-(iba%29) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)
  * [IRAS | Land Intensification Allowance (LIA)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/income-deductions-for-companies/claiming-allowances/land-intensification-allowance-(lia%29) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)
  * [IRAS | Writing-Down Allowances for Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/income-deductions-for-companies/claiming-allowances/writing-down-allowances-for-intellectual-property-rights-(iprs%29) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-capital-allowances-s14n-2022-plus"></a>Section 14N renovation and refurbishment deduction

* **Rule id:** `capital-allowances.s14n.2022-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Qualifying R&amp;R expenditure is deductible over 3 consecutive YAs, with 1-year options for YAs 2021, 2022, 2024 and from YA 2025 onwards. The expenditure cap is S$300,000 per relevant 3-year period.
* **Limits and notes:** IRAS now describes the renovation deduction under section 14N rather than section 14Q. The legacy section 14Q label still appears in an IRAS 'common mistakes' PDF filename.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Tax Treatment of Business Expenses (M-R)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/income-deductions-for-companies/business-expenses/tax-treatment-of-business-expenses-(m-r%29) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-capital-allowances-s19-s19a-2022-plus"></a>Sections 19 and 19A capital allowances

* **Rule id:** `capital-allowances.s19-s19a.2022-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** IRAS allows qualifying fixed assets to be written off over 1 year, 2 years (for YAs 2021, 2022 and 2024), 3 years, or the prescribed/elected working life, with balancing adjustments on disposal.
* **Limits and notes:** The module focuses on cash acquisitions and straight-line schedules; caller-supplied reviewed totals are preferable for complex hire-purchase or transfer cases.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Capital Allowances](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/income-deductions-for-companies/claiming-allowances/capital-allowances) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

### <a id="area-sg-corporate-tax"></a>Corporate income tax (6)

#### <a id="rule-sg-cit-rebates-2024-2026"></a>CIT rebates and cash grants for YA 2024 to YA 2026

* **Rule id:** `cit.rebates.2024-2026`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2024 to 31 Dec 2026
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** IRAS currently lists 50% CIT rebates for YA 2024 to YA 2026, capped at S$40,000 less any cash grant where applicable. YA 2026 narrative confirms the active-company and local-employee conditions for the cash grant.
* **Limits and notes:** The current IRAS page states the detailed cash-grant conditions in the YA 2026 section; this module applies the same structure to YA 2024 and YA 2025 because the current rebate table preserves the same 'less cash grant where applicable' mechanics. No primary-source YA 2027 rebate has been verified in this module.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Corporate Income Tax Rate, Rebates &amp; Tax Exemption Schemes](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/basics-of-corporate-income-tax/corporate-income-tax-rate-rebates-and-tax-exemption-schemes) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-allocation-exempt-income-disallowance-2022-plus"></a>Expenses attributable to exempt, non-taxable or foreign exempt income are not deductible against Singapore taxable income

* **Rule id:** `allocation.exempt-income-disallowance.2022-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** The allocation engine supports direct attribution, gross revenue, asset value, property count and fixed-percentage policies so that disallowed expenses are segregated from taxable Singapore income.
* **Limits and notes:** Allocation bases are configurable policy choices rather than statute-set apportionment formulas; overrides should be reviewed and retained in the audit trail.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Preparing a Tax Computation](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/form-c-s-form-c-s-(lite%29-form-c-filing/preparing-a-tax-computation) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)
  * [IRAS | Companies Receiving Foreign Income](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/income-deductions-for-companies/companies-receiving-foreign-income) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-tax-computation-preparing-tax-computation-2022-plus"></a>IRAS tax computation flow

* **Rule id:** `tax-computation.preparing-tax-computation.2022-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** The computation starts from accounting profit, adjusts for non-taxable income and disallowable expenses, separates certain investment/foreign income, then applies capital allowances, brought-forward items, donations, tax exemptions and CIT rebates.
* **Limits and notes:** This engine does not model foreign tax credit, group relief or loss carry-back mechanics inside the main statement of taxable income.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Preparing a Tax Computation](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/form-c-s-form-c-s-(lite%29-form-c-filing/preparing-a-tax-computation) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)
  * [IRAS | Unutilised Items (Capital Allowances, Trade Losses &amp; Donations)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/income-deductions-for-companies/unutilised-items-(capital-allowances-trade-losses-donations%29) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)
  * [IRAS | Companies Receiving Foreign Income](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/income-deductions-for-companies/companies-receiving-foreign-income) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)
  * [IRAS | Tax Treatment of Business Expenses (A-F)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/income-deductions-for-companies/business-expenses/tax-treatment-of-business-expenses-(a-f%29) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-cit-pillar-two-info-2025-plus"></a>Pillar Two Domestic Top-up Tax is informational only

* **Rule id:** `cit.pillar-two.info.2025-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2025 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Singapore's IIR and Domestic Top-up Tax apply from financial years starting on or after 1 Jan 2025 for in-scope MNE groups with annual revenue of at least €750 million in at least two of the four preceding financial years.
* **Limits and notes:** The engine only flags potential scope; it does not compute Pillar Two taxes.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Global Anti-Base Erosion (GloBE) Rules and Domestic Top-up Tax (DTT)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/pillar-2-top-up-taxes/global-anti-base-erosion-(globe%29-rules-and-domestic-top-up-tax-(dtt%29) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-cit-rate-and-exemptions-2022-plus"></a>Singapore corporate tax rate and tax exemption schemes

* **Rule id:** `cit.rate-and-exemptions.2022-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Corporate income tax is 17%. New start-up and partial tax exemption schemes are applied on normal chargeable income using IRAS' YA-based bands.
* **Limits and notes:** The detailed shareholder-condition data for SUTE must be supplied by the caller; when omitted, this module does not independently verify beneficial ownership.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Corporate Income Tax Rate, Rebates &amp; Tax Exemption Schemes](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/basics-of-corporate-income-tax/corporate-income-tax-rate-rebates-and-tax-exemption-schemes) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)
  * [IRAS | Basic Guide to Corporate Income Tax for Companies](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/basics-of-corporate-income-tax/basic-guide-to-corporate-income-tax-for-companies) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-cit-reit-trustee-prevailing-rate-2025-plus"></a>Section 43(2) REIT trustee taxable income is modelled at the prevailing corporate tax rate without company-only exemption schemes

* **Rule id:** `cit.reit-trustee-prevailing-rate.2025-plus`
* **Effective:** from 4 Dec 2025 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (secondary source only)
* **What the engine applies:** For REIT trustees, the engine does not apply PTE, SUTE or CIT rebate when the taxpayer is modelled as a non-company entity; taxable income is charged at the prevailing corporate tax rate.
* **Limits and notes:** This is an engine interpretation of para 6.1's 'prevailing corporate tax rate' wording for trustee-level taxable income, read together with the company-only nature of PTE, SUTE and CIT rebates.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS e-Tax Guide | Income Tax Treatment of REITs and Approved Sub-Trusts (Twelfth Edition)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/docs/default-source/e-tax/e-taxguide_income-tax-treatment-of-reits-and-approved-sub-trusts.pdf) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-gst-registration-and-penalties-2022-plus"></a>GST registration, filing due dates and late penalties

* **Rule id:** `gst.registration-and-penalties.2022-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** The engine models the S$1 million registration threshold, the 2025-07-01 prospective-registration timing change, the F5 due-date helpers, the GIRO deduction timing, late-filing composition fees and late-payment penalties.

#### <a id="rule-sg-reit-tax-filing-2022-plus"></a>REIT Form UT and Section 45G filing mechanics

* **Rule id:** `reit-tax.filing.2022-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (secondary source only)
* **What the engine applies:** The trustee files Form UT with audited accounts and tax computation by 15 April each year. The guide states there is no need to file ECI, and the engine continues to expose the Section 45G remittance helper for distributions.
* **Limits and notes:** Form UT and the no-ECI position are directly stated in paragraph 16.1 of the guide. The Section 45G remittance helper remains mechanically set to the 15th of the second month from payment, but users should confirm the operational filing screen / notice wording where needed.
* **Sources:**

#### <a id="rule-sg-identifiers-pdpc-masking"></a>Prefer masked NRIC/FIN handling

#### <a id="rule-sg-identifiers-gst-registration-format"></a>GST registration number format

### <a id="area-sg-other"></a>Other (3)

#### <a id="rule-sg-badges-of-trade-iras-factors"></a>IRAS badges of trade factors for gains from sale of real property

* **Rule id:** `badges-of-trade.iras.factors`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** IRAS treats gains as taxable where the facts point to a trade or adventure in the nature of trade. Common factors include acquisition motive, frequency of transactions, length of ownership, supplementary work, financing and sale circumstances.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Sale of property, shares and financial instruments gains](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/gains-from-sale-of-property-shares-and-financial-instruments) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)
  * [IRAS | e-Tax Guide index](https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/e-tax-guides) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-mapping-property-industry-dictionary-2026-10-09"></a>Property-industry chart-of-accounts mapping dictionary

* **Rule id:** `mapping.property-industry-dictionary.2026-10-09`
* **Effective:** from 9 Oct 2026 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Assumption (needs a reviewer's judgement)
* **What the engine applies:** The mapper classifies the statement first (profit and loss versus balance sheet) using explicit wording cues, then applies property-industry category rules and only uses hints / account-code prefixes as weak tie-breakers.
* **Limits and notes:** Precedence rules: receivable / payable / prepaid / accrual / provision-for-liability / deferred-tax-balance cues beat generic income or expense words; conversely explicit 'interest expense', 'interest paid/on', 'income tax expense', 'amortisation of borrowing costs' and similar P&amp;L cues beat loan-account wording. Unknown names always return low-confidence suggestions (0.30 or below).
* **Sources:**
  * [Internal mapping policy informed by IRAS tax-computation categories and common property-industry COA naming](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/form-c-s-form-c-s-(lite%29-form-c-filing/preparing-a-tax-computation) (IRAS + project mapping policy, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-badges-of-trade-scoring-assumption"></a>Transparent scoring model for badges-of-trade assessment

* **Rule id:** `badges-of-trade.scoring.assumption`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Assumption (needs a reviewer's judgement)
* **What the engine applies:** The engine converts qualitative factor assessments into a transparent score for workflow triage.
* **Limits and notes:** IRAS does not publish a numeric scoring system or bright-line thresholds. The score, weights and cut-offs are implementation assumptions for decision support only.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Sale of property, shares and financial instruments gains](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/what-is-taxable-what-is-not/gains-from-sale-of-property-shares-and-financial-instruments) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

### <a id="area-sg-property-tax"></a>Property tax (7)

#### <a id="rule-sg-property-tax-other-10pct"></a>10% rule for non-residential property and vacant land

* **Rule id:** `property-tax.other.10pct`
* **Effective:** No effective dates (applies to every period the engine supports)
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** All non-residential property, vacant land and excluded residential-like classes are taxed at 10% of annual value.
* **Sources:**

#### <a id="rule-sg-property-tax-av-current"></a>Annual value rules for buildings and land

* **Rule id:** `property-tax.av.current`
* **Effective:** No effective dates (applies to every period the engine supports)
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** IRAS assesses annual value by comparable gross rent for buildings and at 5% of estimated freehold market value for land and development sites.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | About Annual Value](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/property-tax/property-owners/annual-value) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)

* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Property Tax Rates and Sample Calculations](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/property-tax/property-owners/property-tax-rates) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-property-tax-rates-ootr-2025"></a>Owner-occupier progressive residential tax rates from 1 Jan 2025

* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2025 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)

* **Rule id:** `property-tax.rebates.2023-2026`

* **Effective:** No effective dates (applies to every period the engine supports)
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)

* **Rule id:** `property-tax.private-apportionment.assumption`
* **Effective:** No effective dates (applies to every period the engine supports)
* **Confidence:** Assumption (needs a reviewer's judgement)
* **What the engine applies:** The engine prorates annual tax by calendar days for part-year ownership and occupancy changes as a practical reconciliation convention.

### <a id="area-sg-reit-tax"></a>REIT &amp; fund distributions (2)

#### <a id="rule-sg-reit-distribution-policy-allocation-2022-plus"></a>REIT distribution policy, holder allocation and withholding reconciliation

* **Rule id:** `reit-distribution.policy-allocation.2022-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** The engine allocates declared REIT distributions across tax-transparent, trustee-taxed, tax-exempt and capital buckets, then allocates those amounts across holders with deterministic largest-remainder cents reconciliation and investor-class withholding.
* **Limits and notes:** Per-holder rounding is a product-engine policy choice rather than an IRAS formula. The engine uses largest-remainder allocation so totals always reconcile exactly to the declared cents.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Income Tax Treatment of REITs and Approved Sub-Trusts (Twelfth Edition)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/docs/default-source/e-tax/e-taxguide_income-tax-treatment-of-reits-and-approved-sub-trusts.pdf) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-reit-tax-transparency-and-distribution-2022-plus"></a>REIT tax-transparency, trustee taxation, rollover adjustments and return-of-capital treatment

* **Rule id:** `reit-tax.transparency-and-distribution.2022-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** The engine models the 90% same-year distribution condition, specified-income transparency, rollover income adjustments, trustee-level taxation of retained / non-specified income, and the distinction between tax-transparent, trustee-taxed, tax-exempt and capital distributions.
* **Limits and notes:** The engine conservatively treats a failure of the 90% threshold as a worst-case transparency denial for the period's specified income.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Income Tax Treatment of REITs and Approved Sub-Trusts (Twelfth Edition)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/docs/default-source/e-tax/e-taxguide_income-tax-treatment-of-reits-and-approved-sub-trusts.pdf) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

### <a id="area-sg-stamp-duty"></a>Stamp duty (BSD / ABSD / SSD / lease) (8)

#### <a id="rule-sg-stamp-duty-absd-trust-refund"></a>ABSD (Trust) refund for identifiable individual beneficiaries

* **Rule id:** `stamp-duty.absd.trust.refund`
* **Effective:** from 9 May 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** ABSD (Trust) of 65% is paid upfront and may be refunded down to the highest direct-purchase ABSD profile where the trust is for identifiable individual beneficiaries only and the application is made within 6 months.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Remission of ABSD (Trust)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/appeals-refunds-reliefs-and-remissions/common-stamp-duty-remissions-and-reliefs-for-property/remission-of-absd-(trust%29) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-stamp-duty-absd-2023-04-27"></a>ABSD rates from 27 Apr 2023

* **Rule id:** `stamp-duty.absd.2023-04-27`
* **Effective:** from 27 Apr 2023 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** The current ABSD regime charges 20/30% for SC second/third+, 5/30/35% for SPR first/second/third+, 60% for foreigners, 65% for entities, 65% for trustees and 40% gross for housing developers (5% non-remittable plus 35% remittable subject to conditions).
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/buying-or-acquiring-property/additional-buyer's-stamp-duty-(absd%29) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-stamp-duty-bsd-2018-2023"></a>BSD differentiated residential and non-residential rates from 20 Feb 2018

* **Rule id:** `stamp-duty.bsd.2018-2023`
* **Effective:** from 20 Feb 2018 to 14 Feb 2023
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Residential property uses the 1/2/3/4% tiers from 20 Feb 2018 to 14 Feb 2023; non-residential property remained capped at 3% in that period.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/buying-or-acquiring-property/buyer's-stamp-duty-(bsd%29) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-stamp-duty-bsd-2023-02-15"></a>BSD higher marginal rates from 15 Feb 2023

* **Rule id:** `stamp-duty.bsd.2023-02-15`
* **Effective:** from 15 Feb 2023 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** From 15 Feb 2023, residential BSD extends to 5% and 6% marginal tiers and non-residential BSD extends to a 5% top rate.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/buying-or-acquiring-property/buyer's-stamp-duty-(bsd%29) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-stamp-duty-ssd-industrial-2013-01-12"></a>Industrial SSD from 12 Jan 2013

* **Rule id:** `stamp-duty.ssd.industrial.2013-01-12`
* **Effective:** from 12 Jan 2013 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Industrial SSD applies for up to 3 years at 15%, 10% and 5% on the higher of price and market value.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD) for Industrial Property](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/selling-or-disposing-property/seller's-stamp-duty-(ssd%29-for-industrial-property) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-stamp-duty-lease-current"></a>Lease duty on immovable-property tenancy agreements

* **Rule id:** `stamp-duty.lease.current`
* **Effective:** No effective dates (applies to every period the engine supports)
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Lease duty is exempt where AAR does not exceed S$1,000 and otherwise applies at 0.4% of total rent for terms of 4 years or less or 0.4% of 4 times AAR for longer or indefinite terms. Premiums are charged at BSD rates.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Renting a Property](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/renting-a-property) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-stamp-duty-ssd-residential-2025-07-04"></a>Residential SSD holding period and rates from 4 Jul 2025

* **Rule id:** `stamp-duty.ssd.residential.2025-07-04`
* **Effective:** from 4 Jul 2025 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** For residential properties acquired on or after 4 Jul 2025, SSD applies for up to 4 years at 16%, 12%, 8% and 4% tiers.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD) for Residential Property](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/selling-or-disposing-property/seller's-stamp-duty-(ssd%29-for-residential-property) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-stamp-duty-deadlines-current"></a>Stamping deadlines and late-payment penalties

* **Rule id:** `stamp-duty.deadlines.current`
* **Effective:** No effective dates (applies to every period the engine supports)
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Signed-in-Singapore documents must be stamped within 14 days; overseas-signed documents within 30 days after first receipt in Singapore. Late penalties are S$10 or duty if up to 3 months late and S$25 or 4 times duty if over 3 months late.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | When to Pay Stamp Duty](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/paying-stamp-duty/when-to-pay-stamp-duty) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)
  * [IRAS | Late Payment or Non-Payment of Stamp Duty](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/paying-stamp-duty/late-payment-of-stamp-duty) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

### <a id="area-sg-withholding-tax"></a>Withholding tax (6)

#### <a id="rule-sg-withholding-tax-rates-current"></a>Core Section 45 withholding tax rates

* **Rule id:** `withholding-tax.rates.current`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** This module models the main domestic WHT rates visible on the IRAS withholding-tax pages as at 2026-10-09: interest 15%, royalties 10%, director's fees 24%, technical/service/management fees at the prevailing corporate rate (17% currently for companies), non-resident professional gross withholding 15%, rent of movable property 15%, non-resident public entertainers 15%, and branch remittance nil.
* **Limits and notes:** This module does not separately model the professional net-income election or the REIT-distribution withholding categories shown on the IRAS rates page.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Types of Payment and Withholding Tax (WHT) Rates](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/withholding-tax/basics-of-withholding-tax/types-of-payment-and-withholding-tax-rates) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)
  * [IRAS | Payments that are Subject to Withholding Tax](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/withholding-tax/payments-to-non-resident-company/payments-that-are-subject-to-withholding-tax) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)
  * [IRAS | Tax obligations for non-resident professional](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/withholding-tax/payments-to-non-resident-professional-(consultant-trainer-coach-etc-%29/tax-obligations-for-non-resident-professional) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)
  * [IRAS | Tax for Non-Resident Directors](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/withholding-tax/payments-to-non-resident-director/tax-obligations-for-non-resident-director) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)
  * [IRAS | Tax obligations of non-resident public entertainer](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/withholding-tax/payments-to-non-resident-public-entertainer-(artiste-musician-sportsman-etc-%29/tax-obligations-of-non-resident-public-entertainer) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-withholding-tax-penalty-current"></a>Late-payment penalties for WHT

* **Rule id:** `withholding-tax.penalty.current`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** IRAS imposes a 5% late-payment penalty and, if the tax is still unpaid 30 days after the due date, an additional 1% for every completed month it remains unpaid, the additional penalty capped at 15% of the unpaid tax (so at most 20% in all).
* **Limits and notes:** The engine counts completed calendar months from 30 days after the due date, as in IRAS's worked example, and treats the 5% penalty as imposed at the due date. The Act counts from the imposition of the 5% penalty, which can be later; check the penalty notice.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Late payment and non-payment of taxes (worked example: S$7,000 due 15 Jul 2025, paid 25 Oct 2025, penalty S$490)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/withholding-tax/withholding-tax-payments/late-payment-and-non-payment-of-taxes) (IRAS, read 19 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-reit-tax-withholding-and-declarations-2022-plus"></a>REIT investor-class withholding and declaration rules

* **Rule id:** `reit-tax.withholding-and-declarations.2022-plus`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Individuals, Singapore-incorporated entities, qualifying Singapore branches, specified Singapore bodies, qualifying international organisations and qualifying REIT ETFs receive no tax deduction; qualifying non-resident non-individuals and qualifying non-resident funds get 10% final withholding within the concession windows; other non-resident non-individuals are withheld at the prevailing corporate rate.
* **Limits and notes:** The 10% concessions are modelled through 31 Dec 2030. Form A (Declaration for Singapore Tax Purposes) and Form B (Declaration by Depository Agents) are treated as the practical support for applying zero-deduction or concessionary treatment; paragraph 12.2(b) requires withholding where the beneficiary's status is not confirmed.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Income Tax Treatment of REITs and Approved Sub-Trusts (Twelfth Edition)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/docs/default-source/e-tax/e-taxguide_income-tax-treatment-of-reits-and-approved-sub-trusts.pdf) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

* **Rule id:** `withholding-tax.service-place.current`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Management, technical-assistance, consultancy and professional fees are generally subject to WHT only to the extent the services are rendered in Singapore unless a deeming rule or incentive changes the outcome.
* **Sources:**
  * [IRAS | Tax obligations for non-resident professional](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/withholding-tax/payments-to-non-resident-professional-(consultant-trainer-coach-etc-%29/tax-obligations-for-non-resident-professional) (IRAS, read 9 Oct 2026)

#### <a id="rule-sg-withholding-tax-deadline-current"></a>WHT remittance due date

* **Rule id:** `withholding-tax.deadline.current`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Verified (primary source)
* **What the engine applies:** Withholding tax is due to IRAS by the 15th day of the second month from the date of payment to the non-resident.

#### <a id="rule-sg-withholding-tax-treaty-override"></a>Treaty override input

* **Rule id:** `withholding-tax.treaty.override`
* **Effective:** from 1 Jan 2022 until further notice
* **Confidence:** Assumption (needs a reviewer's judgement)
* **What the engine applies:** The engine accepts a treaty rate override but does not embed any treaty table or beneficial-ownership logic.
* **Limits and notes:** Users must confirm treaty entitlement outside the engine before passing treatyRateBps.
